prompt: Use an instructor-provided held-back disposable local incident, or a learner-created case kept unseen until the independence gate, that is materially different from every LES-0033 guided and answered scenario. It must include ambiguous user impact, misleading or missing telemetry, at least two failure domains, concurrent responders, a severity decision, competing mitigations with one dangerous attractive option, stakeholder pressure, an incomplete recovery signal, a shift boundary, and evidence for a causal review. After the independence gate, do not open ASM-0082, ASM-0083, the lesson complete-answer or interview sections, or generated solutions. Lead a timed simulated response and submit sanitized evidence from page receipt through action closure design. No real page, production, provider, employer, ticket, chat, email, identity, or customer system may be contacted.
deliverables: Completed independence, authorization, environment, accessibility, help, and sanitization gate before analysis
First-five-minute record with responder fitness, page identity, acknowledgement, independent user-impact evidence, population, interval, scope, correctness, trend, and uncertainty
Severity and declaration decision tied to an explicit local policy plus reassessment triggers
Acknowledged incident-command, operations, communications, planning, specialist, and escalation role map with authority boundaries
Canonical incident-state document containing objective, impact, roles, facts, hypotheses, assumptions, decisions, changes, communications, risks, and checkpoints
At least six ranked falsifiable hypotheses with confirming and rejecting evidence at named boundaries
At least four mitigation candidates compared for time-to-relief, reversibility, blast radius, confidence, evidence preservation, data/security risk, cost, and authorization
Two complete controlled-change proposals with owner, target, preconditions, expected evidence, deadline, abort, rollback, and result recording plus one explicit dangerous-action rejection
Internal responder, customer-safe, and executive updates with timestamps, facts, uncertainty, workaround where valid, owner, and next-update commitment
Live STATE handoff record with sender, receiver, restatement, access check, explicit acceptance, broadcast, and fatigue or staffing assessment
Service-specific recovery predicate covering journeys, cohorts, correctness, queues, dependencies, capacity, telemetry validity, temporary state, and observation window
Verified timeline and causal graph with at least five mechanism links and explicit contributing conditions rather than one-person blame
At least six owned actions spanning prevention, containment, detection, mitigation, recovery, coordination, or human sustainability with due dates and acceptance tests
Five-minute product-company interview defense plus at least fifteen technically specific non-claims
Exact cleanup inventory and proof that every resource permitted by the local simulation is absent
evidenceRequirements: The case was unseen and materially different from all published LES-0033 guided and answered material
The learner records every hint, tool, reference, AI assistance, peer input, and accessibility accommodation used
No personal names, employer names, customer information, secrets, internal URLs, private paths, real incident identifiers, messages, screenshots, logs, or confidential architecture are submitted
All timestamps name timezone and clock source; ordering conflicts and uncertainty remain visible
User impact is not inferred solely from process, pod, node, provider, or alert health
Severity is mapped to stated impact policy and revised when evidence changes
Every role is explicitly acknowledged and every production-like mutation is serialized through the simulated operations path
Facts, hypotheses, assumptions, decisions, and outcomes are separately labeled
Every proposed change includes authority, scope, prediction, abort, rollback or recovery, evidence preservation, and independent user validation
Communication contains no invented root cause, ETA, blame, secret, contractual interpretation, or unsupported all-user claim
Handoff includes live receipt, restatement, access, fatigue, commitments, risks, and public role transfer
Recovery is not inferred from alert reset, one dashboard, one process state, or change completion
The causal review includes trigger, latent conditions, propagation, failed defenses, detection, mitigation, and organizational context without removing accountability
Actions identify risk, owner, priority, due date, acceptance test, verification evidence, and a closure mechanism
No production, shared, employer, cloud, Kubernetes, ticket, chat, email, pager, identity, status, security, legal, or customer system is modified or contacted
Cleanup proves exact absence of every allowed file, process, socket, port, container, namespace, queue, and temporary resource
A qualified reviewer confirms answer isolation, safe scope, evidence integrity, reasoning quality, proof limits, remediation, and delayed reassessment

rubric.observableEvidence: Unseen case, declared help, safe local scope, sanitization, timestamps, and no answer leakage.
User-first evidence, uncertainty, trend, policy mapping, and reassessment are explicit.
Acknowledged roles, escalation, bounded specialists, canonical state, and no freelancing.
At least six falsifiable explanations use confirming/rejecting evidence and preserve proof limits.
Candidates and controlled changes address relief, reversibility, blast radius, abort, rollback, data, security, and cost.
Three audiences receive useful facts, uncertainty, action, workaround, owner, and next update without fabrication.
Live STATE transfer, restatement, access, acceptance, broadcast, fatigue, and staffing controls are evidenced.
Journey, correctness, backlog, dependency, capacity, telemetry, observation, and temporary-state gates are defensible.
Mechanism graph and at least six owned, prioritized, testable risk-reducing actions avoid shallow blame.
Clear senior defense, fifteen precise limits, and exact local absence proof.
